new.title: Pair beer and cheese at De Markies
new.desc: This speciality beer café keeps more than 250 bottled beers and 12 rotating taps, plus a cheese menu of 17 cheeses with a flavour wheel to help you match them. Vintage enamel beer signs cover the walls, and the sunny terrace seats a hundred with a view of the theatre. Twice a year it organises the Leeuwarden Beer Festival.
new.tip: It is closed on Monday and opens in the afternoon on other days. Tell the bar what you usually drink and let them choose for you.

new.title: Have coffee in the hall of the old post office
new.desc: The monumental hall of Leeuwarden's former post office is now the grand café of Post-Plaza, which opened in December 2015. A glass passage links it to the old bank building next door, and hotel rooms fill the floors above.
new.tip: It works at any hour: breakfast, lunch, high tea or a late drink. Look up at the hall before you sit down.

new.title: Take a terrace seat at De Walrus
new.desc: Grand café De Walrus opened in 2009 on the Gouverneursplein, in buildings that earlier housed the Leeuwarder Bankvereeniging, the furniture factory Bearda and a library. It is an all-day address in the heart of the city, for coffee and cake, lunch or drinks after work.
new.tip: On warm days the terrace on the square fills up fast, so come early. It is a short walk from the Jacobijnerkerk.

new.title: Say hello to Us Mem, the mother of all Frisian cows
new.desc: Us Mem, Frisian for 'Our Mother', is a bronze cow by sculptor Gerhardus Jan Adema, made a quarter larger than life. Dairy farmers gave her to the Frisian cattle herd book for its 75th anniversary in 1954, as a portrait of the ideal pedigree cow. She stood on the Zuiderplein until 1990, when she moved to her little roundabout on the Harlingersingel.
new.tip: She is a couple of minutes on foot from the Oldehove, so combine the two.

new.title: Admire the gable of the Kanselarij
new.desc: The Kanselarij was built between 1566 and 1571, probably on the orders of Philip II, as the seat of the Court of Friesland. It is one of the best preserved brick Gothic buildings in the north that is not a church. Nine statues crown the gable, with Justice and other virtues below a figure of divine providence. It later served as a hospital, a barracks, a library and the Frisian resistance museum.
new.tip: On the steps of 1621 look for the four stone lions holding the shields of the quarters of Friesland.

new.title: Join the home crowd at SC Cambuur
new.desc: SC Cambuur, the football club of Leeuwarden, moved in 2024 into the Kooi Stadion on the west side of town, after sixty years at the old Cambuurstadion. The new ground holds 15,000 people, about half as many again as the old one, and saw its first match on 18 August 2024.
new.tip: Buy tickets online in advance. The stadium is a short bike or bus ride from the centre.

new.title: See a band at Neushoorn
new.desc: Neushoorn is the pop venue of Leeuwarden, in a building on the Ruiterskwartier that once housed a bicycle and car works and later a garage. From 1991 the nightclub Rock It made it the heart of local nightlife, and a tribute to the club hangs in the sound lock of the main hall. Besides concerts and club nights it has five rehearsal rooms, two dance studios and its own café.
new.tip: The café is a good place to start the evening. Check the programme online, as popular shows sell out.

new.title: Drink a harbour-brewed ale at Het Brouwdok in Harlingen
new.desc: Het Brouwdok brews Frisian craft beer in a former timber shed on the Nieuwe Willemskade, on the seaward side of the dike. The brewers call their beer seaworthy and brewed outside the dikes, and the taproom looks out towards the Wadden Sea.
new.tip: It makes a good stop before or after the ferry to Vlieland or Terschelling. Book ahead if you want a tour of the brewery.

new.title: Sip a Nobeltje where it was invented on Ameland
new.desc: Nobeltje is the sweet, strong liqueur of Ameland, first mixed by Willem Barend Nobel, who opened a café in Ballum around 1900. The family story goes back to the bitter winter of 1902, when islanders came home frozen from a sleigh race in Holwerd and needed warming up. Four generations on, the Nobel family still runs the hotel, the restaurant and a tasting room in the village.
new.tip: Drink it neat after dinner. The family's shop in Ballum sells bottles to take home.

new.title: Have a drink in the taproom of Hotel van der Werff
new.desc: The best known address on Schiermonnikoog began in 1726 as the island's court house, town hall and post house, on the corner of the Reeweg. It has been a hotel for more than a century, and marked its hundredth year in 2014 with a book about its history. In the old taproom a carved coat of arms of the Stachouwer family, once lords of the island, is set high in the wall.
new.tip: You do not have to be a hotel guest to sit in the taproom or eat in the restaurant. Look for the stone in the wall, said to come from a castle that the sea swallowed around 1700.
new.q: Hotel van der Werff Reeweg 2 Schiermonnikoog

new.title: Photograph the Waterpoort, the emblem of Sneek
new.desc: Two eight-sided towers joined by a bridge with a gatekeeper's house on top: the Waterpoort has guarded the water entrance to Sneek since around 1492 and got its decorative look in 1613. The town's other gates were all pulled down in the nineteenth century, and this one survived thanks to public pressure. It appears on the ace of spades in Dutch playing cards.
new.tip: The classic view is across the water of De Kolk. The Elfstedentocht route passes right by, and Sneekweek opens here with a parade of boats.

new.title: Stand under the glass roof of the Broerekerk in Bolsward
new.desc: The Franciscans built this three-aisled friary church in the thirteenth century. A fire on 8 May 1980 left it a roofless ruin, and in 2006 architect Jelle de Jong covered the old walls with a roof of glass. The result is half church, half courtyard, with the sky above the Gothic arches, and it is now used for events.
new.tip: Go on a bright day, when the roof frame draws shadows across the brick. It may be closed to visitors during private events.

new.title: Climb the highest terp in the country at Hegebeintum
new.desc: The mound of Hegebeintum rises 8.80 metres above sea level, the highest terp in the Netherlands and Germany. Between 1870 and 1928 much of it was dug away and sold as fertile soil, which is why the little church of the eleventh or twelfth century now stands on a steep green island. Inside hang the mourning boards of noble families.
new.tip: The church is not freely open: ask at the visitor centre at the foot of the terp. Bring a jacket, as there is nothing up there to stop the wind.

new.title: Paddle the peat lakes of De Alde Feanen
new.desc: National park De Alde Feanen, the 'old fens', is a maze of water and marsh left behind by centuries of peat digging, whose long narrow pits filled up with water. About 180 bird species have been recorded here, storks nest at It Eibertshiem, and otters were brought back in 2011. The visitor centre De Wiidpleats in Earnewâld shares a site with the Frisian agricultural museum.
new.tip: Start at the visitor centre for route maps. A canoe or quiet boat gets you much closer to the birds than the paths do.

new.title: Sail into the party of Sneekweek
new.desc: Since 1934 Sneek has hosted what is called the largest sailing event on inland waters in Europe. It starts each year on the Friday before the first Saturday of August, with a fleet parade past the Waterpoort and through the canals. Hundreds of boats then race for days on the Sneekermeer, coordinated from the Starteiland in the middle of the lake.
new.tip: Take the ferry to the Starteiland to watch the racing from the shore. Wednesday is Hardzeildag, traditionally a day off for many people in Sneek.

new.title: Walk the cliff edge at Oudemirdum
new.desc: Friesland is flat, except in Gaasterland, where the land ice of the Saalian ice age pushed up a ridge of boulder clay. At the Oudemirdumer Klif that ridge ends at the IJsselmeer in a grassy cliff about 1,400 metres long, protected by Natuurmonumenten since 1927. Harebells flower on the slope and sand martins breed here.
new.tip: Follow the footpath down to the cliff towards evening, when the light over the water is at its best. The woods of Gaasterland just inland make it an easy half-day outing.
